comparison: Both evaluations strongly support the core findings on color opponency in V1 centers (C1, C12, C14, C15). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative validation (33% variance, 33.1% color-opponent neurons), while peer reviewers affirm this as 'solid characterization' and a key contribution. Complete agreement on SUPPORTED status.

OpenEval R1 includes surround findings (C2, C13) showing luminance dominance (82% variance). Peer R2 accepts these surround properties as part of the solid characterization without challenge. Both SUPPORTED, with OpenEval providing more quantitative detail.

Both strongly support the posterior-anterior asymmetry in color processing (C3, C23, C24, C25, C86). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative evidence (twice as much color variance posteriorly) and reproducibility across animals. Peer reviewers treat this as a key contribution, explicitly affirming 'more numerous in upper visual field.' Complete agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Both support the clustering analysis and differential distribution of response types (C31, C32, C33, C34, C88, C89, C90). OpenEval emphasizes GMM methodology (89.2% accuracy) and mechanistic explanation. Peer reviewers affirm the clustering approach and spatial distribution findings. Complete agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Critical disagreement on evaluation type. OpenEval rates predator detection interpretation (C6, C35-C38, C67) as UNCERTAIN, noting model limitations and lack of behavioral validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the modeling work provides 'insight into ethological relevance' while acknowledging speculative nature. Both recognize speculation but differ on confidence level.

Both strongly support light-level dependency findings (C21, C22, C43, C80, C81, C83, C84, C85). OpenEval provides detailed analysis ruling out signal-to-noise explanations. Peer reviewers affirm 'opponent responses more pronounced at photopic light levels' without challenge. Complete agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Both support the comparative retinal-V1 analysis (C19, C20, C75, C76) showing greater color opponency in V1 (33%) versus retina (12%). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative comparison while noting speculative mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept the comparison and inference, framing mechanistic limitations as future work rather than critique. Agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Both support claims about photopic color representation and rod contributions (C43, C44, C45). OpenEval emphasizes appropriate caveats about photoreceptor contributions. Peer R13 accepts these as part of overall characterization. Agreement on SUPPORTED status with overlapping claims C44, C45.

Both support the decoding analysis methodology (C77, C79). OpenEval emphasizes SVM cross-validation and statistical testing. Peer reviewers praise the experimental approach and dataset quality. Agreement on SUPPORTED status, though peer review focuses more broadly on overall methods.

Both support the clustering methodology and validation (C28, C29, C91). OpenEval provides detailed validation metrics (89.2% accuracy, cross-validation). Peer reviewers accept clustering analysis and consistency across animals as convincing evidence. Complete agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Both support the acknowledgment of methodological limitations (C49, C50). OpenEval frames this as appropriate scientific caution with evidence of reasonable effectiveness. Peer reviewers note revisions 'nicely clarified limitations' and emphasize strengths. Agreement on SUPPORTED status for transparent limitation reporting.

Both strongly support the connection to natural scene statistics and adaptive interpretation (C26, C51, C52, C53, C87). OpenEval notes cautious language ('might be') and grounding in prior literature. Peer reviewers accept the ethological relevance argument as a strength. Complete agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Both support background claims about mouse photoreceptor biology and color discrimination (C7-C11). OpenEval treats these as appropriately cited factual context. Peer reviewers accept background framework without challenge. Agreement on SUPPORTED status for established knowledge.

Both support methodological validation claims (C72, C73, C74). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative validation of stimulus alignment. Peer R9 accepts methodological approach and validation procedures. Agreement on SUPPORTED status with partial claim overlap.

Both support experimental methodology (C69, C70, C71). OpenEval focuses on specific validation procedures. Peer R11 praises large-scale imaging approach and dataset quality. Agreement on SUPPORTED status with complementary emphasis.

Both support background claims on comparative color vision mechanisms (C39-C42). OpenEval treats these as appropriately cited literature providing context. Peer reviewers accept background framework without challenge. Agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Both support claims about residual color encoding and spatial distribution (C46, C47). OpenEval notes appropriate cautious language for functional interpretation (C48). Peer R13 accepts these as part of solid characterization. Agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Both support claims about retinal/LGN processing and cortical mechanisms (C54-C57). OpenEval emphasizes speculative but reasonable inference connecting retinal mechanisms to V1. Peer reviewers accept comparative analysis without challenge. Agreement on SUPPORTED status.

Both support comparative neuroscience background claims (C58-C63). OpenEval treats these as appropriately cited literature contextualizing distributed processing. Peer reviewers accept background framework as established knowledge. Agreement on SUPPORTED status.

OpenEval rates functional interpretations about predator detection and ethological relevance (C64-C68) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of behavioral validation, despite logical reasoning. Peer R10 accepts background claims (C64-C66) as established knowledge without specific evaluation of speculative aspects. Partial overlap with different evaluation focus.

OpenEval rates modeling-based functional interpretations (C92-C95) as UNCERTAIN, noting behavioral relevance remains untested despite logical reasoning. Peer R6 accepts modeling work (C94, C95) as SUPPORTED, providing insight into ethological relevance. Disagreement on confidence level for speculative functional claims.

Both support validation of experimental approach (C16-C18). OpenEval emphasizes recovery of known V1 properties validates the paradigm. Peer R11 praises the large-scale imaging methodology. Agreement on SUPPORTED status with complementary focus on validation aspects.

OpenEval R8 supports decoding analysis showing color discriminability patterns (C77, C78, C79). Peer R2 accepts center-surround differences (C78, C82) as part of solid characterization. Agreement on SUPPORTED status with minimal claim overlap.
